response.sql:
WITH media_type_rates AS (
  SELECT 
    mt.Name,
    SUM(t.Bytes) * 1.0 / SUM(t.Milliseconds) AS rate
  FROM MediaType mt
  INNER JOIN Track t ON mt.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId AND t.Bytes IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY mt.MediaTypeId, mt.Name
),
average_rate AS (
  SELECT AVG(rate) AS avg_rate
  FROM media_type_rates
)
SELECT 
  mtr.Name,
  mtr.rate,
  mtr.rate - ar.avg_rate AS exceeds
FROM media_type_rates mtr
CROSS JOIN average_rate ar
WHERE mtr.rate > ar.avg_rate
ORDER BY mtr.Name;

assumptions.assumption: Tracks with NULL Bytes are excluded from rate calculations. The phrase 'counting only tracks that have a media type' refers to non-NULL MediaTypeId, but calculating bytes-per-millisecond requires non-NULL Bytes, so these are necessarily excluded.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat NULL Bytes as 0 when calculating media-type rates, including all tracks that have a non-NULL MediaTypeId regardless of Bytes value.

  SELECT 
    mt.Name,
    SUM(COALESCE(t.Bytes, 0)) * 1.0 / SUM(t.Milliseconds) AS rate
  FROM MediaType mt
  INNER JOIN Track t ON mt.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId
  GROUP BY mt.MediaTypeId, mt.Name
),
average_rate AS (
  SELECT AVG(rate) AS avg_rate
  FROM media_type_rates
)
SELECT 
  mtr.Name,
  mtr.rate,
  mtr.rate - ar.avg_rate AS exceeds
FROM media_type_rates mtr
CROSS JOIN average_rate ar
WHERE mtr.rate > ar.avg_rate
ORDER BY mtr.Name;
